t: This is a statue of Francis Bacon at Gray's Inn. Bacon was an English philosopher and statesman who served as Attorney General and then Lord Chancellor under King James I. He argued for the importance of natural philosophy, guided by the scientific method, and his works stayed influential throughout the Scientific Revolution. The statue was made by the sculptor F. W. Pomeroy, a leading figure in the New Sculpture movement, which turned towards naturalism. Pomeroy's other London work includes the figure of Lady Justice on the dome of the Old Bailey.
